helpPageTitle.message: What to do after a scam – CyberGuard

helpTitle.message: A scammer may have my data – what now?

helpIntro.message: Stay calm, this can happen to anyone. Go through the steps below right away. The sooner, the better.

helpBankTitle.message: Card, payment code or online banking login

helpBank1.message: Call your bank. You'll find the number on the back of your card or in your banking app. Don't call numbers from texts or e-mails.

helpBank2.message: Ask them to block your card and your online banking access.

helpBank3.message: Check together whether any transfers or payments left your account that you didn't make.

helpPasswordTitle.message: Password for e-mail, a shop or another site

helpPassword1.message: Change the password on the real website, ideally from another computer or phone you trust.

helpPasswordSessions.message: Sign out of all devices (usually in your account settings, under "Security"). If a scammer is already logged in to your account, just changing the password won't kick them out, but this will.

helpPassword2.message: If you use the same password anywhere else, change it there too.

helpPassword3.message: Turn on two-step login (a text or app code) if the site offers it.

helpIdTitle.message: ID number, identity card details or a photo of a document

helpId1.message: In Poland: block your PESEL number in the mObywatel app or on gov.pl (search for "zastrzeż PESEL"). It's free.

helpId2.message: Report your ID card at any bank (Dokumenty Zastrzeżone system) or at your local council office.

helpRemoteTitle.message: Someone told you to install a program (e.g. AnyDesk, TeamViewer)

helpRemote1.message: Disconnect the computer from the internet and ask someone you trust to help remove the program. Through it, the scammer can see your screen and control your computer.

helpReport1.message: Report the page to CERT Polska:

helpReport2.message: In Poland, forward a suspicious text free of charge to 8080.

helpReport3.message: If money is gone, report it to the police too (112).

helpTalkTitle.message: Talk to someone close to you

helpTalk1.message: Scammers scare and rush people so there's no time to think. There's nothing to be ashamed of. It's easier to go through these steps calmly with someone else.

helpCleanText.message: Removes history, cookies, cache and saved form data from the last hour.

helpCleanNote.message: Keep in mind this won't undo what already reached the scammer and won't sign them out of your accounts. The steps above matter most. Afterwards, you'll need to log in again on some sites.

helpCleanDone.message: Done, the last hour has been cleared.

helpCleanDenied.message: The browser didn't give permission, so nothing was removed.

helpCleanFailed.message: That didn't work. You can do it yourself in the browser settings (Ctrl+Shift+Delete).

helpEduSectionTitle.message: Knowledge Base: How attacks work & how to stay safe

helpEduSectionIntro.message: We explain in simple terms how common online threats work and what easy habits will keep you completely safe.

helpTopicPhishingHowText.message: Criminals create sites that look like banks, delivery services (e.g. InPost, postal services), or government portals. They use urgent pressure — threatening account blocks or delivery cancellations to trick you into entering credentials without thinking.

helpTopicPhishingProtectText.message: Remember: banks and institutions never send links demanding urgent logins. Always visit websites by typing their address directly or using bookmarks. Enable two-factor authentication (2FA).

helpTopicLookalikeHowText.message: Scammers register domain names deceptively similar to real brands — swapping letters (like "rn" for "m" or "0" for "o") or using characters from other alphabets (Cyrillic) that look identical on screen.

helpTopicLookalikeProtectText.message: Carefully check the browser address bar. CyberGuard automatically compares the address with the genuine brand and highlights discrepancies.

helpTopicPasswordHowText.message: Many people reuse the same password across multiple sites. When criminals breach an ordinary store or forum, they immediately test that password on email, banking, and social accounts.

helpTopicPasswordProtectText.message: Use a unique password for every critical account (bank, email, identity). CyberGuard monitors your essential passwords and warns you if you start typing a bank password on a foreign site.

helpTopicLinkHowText.message: You see a link displaying the address of a trusted bank, but clicking it takes you to a completely different, malicious server. The visible text does not match the actual destination.

helpTopicLinkProtectText.message: Hover over links before clicking to check the destination URL in the bottom-left corner of your browser. CyberGuard catches these deceptive links automatically.
